- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price drops, model underestimates further decline — add 1–2% buffer below observed drop.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 82.5 for 3+ days, forecast should not rise beyond 83.5 unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward momentum after 10–15 days — apply a 1–3% downward adjustment if sentiment is negative and price has fallen >10% from peak.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to smooth too much — allow 1–2% volatility buffer in forecast.
